The strongest ground is that the promise was oral. Most states require a signed writing to revive a debt that the statute of limitations has barred, so the oral promise to pay the $750 is unenforceable on that basis. Lack of consideration is weaker, because Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 82 makes a promise to pay a limitations-barred debt binding without new consideration, and the overheard "deadbeat" remark is a distractor that neither supplies consideration nor creates duress.

CONFIDENCE: 62
